Replay

Fixed-roster P2P provisioning

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Service ownershipDurability and reconnectScope and acceptance

This package durably enrolls invited members in a deterministic P2P match. It uses replay/provision for enrollment and authenticated process registration, then builds the roster and credentials required by replay/p2p/admission. It does not start a simulation authority lease.

A room has a content ID, unique session ID and durable player count (2–8). The first enrollee administers invitations and creates the signaling room; every participant has the same simulation role. All grants have can_host, trusted_authority and infrastructure false. Those flags describe authority permissions, not the ability to listen for P2P transport connections.

Service ownership#

Use one stable, serialized Hub per bounded deployment. hub_open loads the entire existing room inventory before accepting requests; it refuses a player count/content mismatch. hub_receive accepts the existing provisioning protocol (Create, Invite, Join, Revoke). Existing provision.Client, Enrollment_Journal and Godot Provision_Connection can carry these operations unchanged. The deployment chooses content and player count; public callers cannot choose policy.

Use verified TLS for enrollment because requests contain bearer claims/invites and replies contain private credentials. Transport connection/packet limits are also required. The hub bounds room allocation and uses the same global and per-connection enrollment token buckets as the authority provisioning hub.

hub_control_receive routes only authenticated Query, Challenge and Rebind. It filters Start, Renew, nomination, takeover and the optional removal extension before the existing MAC, nonce and sequence verifier. Each record stays at authority epoch zero. Do not expose the embedded enrollment service through the generic authority driver: use the P2P entry points.

Invites reserve their remaining uses against vacant fixed seats. Revoke releases only unused reservations. Existing members never lose/recycle their seat through invite revocation. Exact invite/enrollment retries still work after exhaustion; changing the claim, original endpoint or ticket is a different request. Keys and game tokens are independently generated by the existing enrollment service.

Durability and reconnect#

Bundle wraps the complete private enrollment record plus the fixed player count. The commit callback must atomically compare the previous revision, persist the whole bundle, and reject a changed player count for an existing room. Do not store only bundle.enrollment: that would lose the fixed-roster contract.

The native sqlite package persists the bundle with FULL/WAL transactions, private files, canonical codecs, a separate replay_p2p_provision table, bounded startup inventory and revision checks across service owners. Existing authority room databases are not converted into P2P rooms. Uncertain creation fences the hub; uncertain room mutations fence that room until authoritative storage is reloaded. A committed join whose reply was lost returns the same credential on retry after restart.

After receiving/reloading its grant, a new client process performs authenticated Challenge/Rebind using a fresh RPC nonce. The member ID and key remain stable; the service allocates a newer incarnation. It then queries the current roster. match_from_reply must receive a reply already accepted by auth.Rpc_Client; the helper itself is not a signature verifier. It checks the expected room, content, player count, current local identity, complete enabled membership, and absence of simulation authority.

registry returns Not_Ready until every seat is enrolled. Once complete, it derives an ordered admission roster with session = room ID and P2P admission epoch = 1 for the room's lifetime. A new match requires a new room ID. Rebinds change credentials' incarnations without changing that roster or its code. The public match descriptor contains no peer keys.

For Godot signaling, rendezvous_p2p_room_provider borrows the room and re-reads committed membership on every callback. It stays inactive while enrollment is incomplete, invalidates old incarnations immediately, and refuses a poisoned room. Initialize Rendezvous with mesh=true. Destroy it before its room/hub. Clients can pass the accepted descriptor and their current identity/key to rtc_p2p_config. Multi-room signaling routing remains the deployment's job.

Scope and acceptance#

This supplies bearer room enrollment, not a human account system or matchmaking. It does not change the P2P runner's fixed-roster disconnect/history policy, elect a simulation host, or let late joiners replace departed players.

Run tests/replay_p2p_provision/run.sh for core/wire/client/provider tests and WASM checking, tests/replay_p2p_provision_sqlite/run.sh for storage plus process kills before/after commit, and tests/replay_p2p_provision_service/run.sh for the native Godot TLS service/client fixture. The fixture enrolls three members through one client process. Its results do not cover three-player gameplay or browser execution.

The reusable P2P party owner connects these APIs to Duel's browser and native create/join/rejoin flows. Local tests cover RTC and encrypted ENet gameplay, plus fresh-process archive return. Public deployment, broader recovery and human account integration remain open.
